text_summary: V-204B is a horizontal pressure vessel serving as a knock-out drum on the amine regeneration loop in BAY-2. Design pressure 16 barg, operating temperature range 60–180°C. Contains H2S-rich sour gas under normal operation. Classified as a major-accident hazard vessel under PESO SMPV rules. Nearest safety shower and eye wash station located 12 metres south at emergency station ES-204.

C-14 is a two-stage reciprocating compressor handling mixed hydrocarbon gas at discharge pressures up to 35 barg. Motor-driven, 450 kW, with independent lube oil and seal oil systems. Critical path equipment — loss of C-14 requires plant rate reduction to 60% within 2 hours. Vibration monitoring via online accelerometers at both bearing housings with DCS alarming at 12 mm/s and trip at 18 mm/s.

V-101A is a vertical separator vessel in the crude fractionation unit of BAY-1. Design pressure 10 barg, operating at 7.5 barg under normal conditions. Equipped with pressure relief valve PRV-101 set at 10.0 barg venting to the closed flare header. Internal components include a mesh pad demister and inlet vane distributor. Last internal inspection during 2024 turnaround showed no significant corrosion.

HX-110 is a fixed-tubesheet shell-and-tube heat exchanger providing feed preheat in BAY-1. Shell-side fluid is hot process gas at 310°C; tube-side is incoming crude feed at 120°C. Design conditions: 20 barg shell, 15 barg tube. Known to be susceptible to coke fouling on the tube side, requiring 6-monthly descaling. Tube material is ASTM A213 T11 alloy steel.

T-301 is a fixed-roof atmospheric storage tank for naphtha with a capacity of 2000 m³. Equipped with a nitrogen blanket system maintaining 5 mbar positive pressure. Primary level measurement via guided-wave radar transmitter LT-301A with an independent high-level switch LSHH-301 at 95% capacity. Tank is dyked with a bund wall capable of containing 110% of tank volume. Floating suction arm with vortex breaker installed.

V-302A is a pressure vessel operating as a reflux drum in the distillation section of BAY-3. Design pressure 12 barg, currently operating at 8.2 barg. Material of construction is SA-516 Gr.70 carbon steel with 3 mm corrosion allowance. Accelerated corrosion on the lower shell has been documented since 2022, reducing remaining wall from 12 mm to 8.2 mm. Scheduled for internal coating at the next turnaround in Q4 2025.

R-501 is a catalytic reactor in the hydrocracking unit of BAY-5. Operating temperature range 320–380°C, design pressure 175 barg. Contains a fixed bed of NiMo/Al2O3 catalyst with a design WHSV of 1.5 h⁻¹. Primary cooling via a dedicated cooling water loop with redundant pumps P-501A/B; loss of cooling triggers an automatic quench within 30 seconds. Following the 2023 incident, emergency shutdown logic was upgraded to include independent reactor skin temperature trips.

PP-205 is a centrifugal pump transferring light cycle oil at 12 barg discharge pressure in BAY-2. Single-stage, 75 kW motor-driven, with double mechanical seals operating on API Plan 54 barrier fluid system. Maximum rated flow 150 m³/h. Installed spare PP-205S is available for manual changeover but is not auto-started. Seal flush pressure must be maintained at minimum 2 bar above process to prevent hydrocarbon leakage.
